//: Story Phase 5, chapter 20: Another Terrible Day. The morning after the seven-hundred-percent forecast. The captain's rounds (Pete at the port rail, Gristle at the stores, Salty Jim in the galley, Barnacle Bob in the crew quarters; any order) are each interrupted by the Dead Center, which seems to be following him. Then three bells at the mainmast, Squawks's basket in the way, the last of his down, and the check-in by the cabin door. The Grand Stenchmaster spends the whole chapter in his chair, facing a sheet.

start: Your bed. Feather mattress, red wool blanket, and a faint yellow outline on the pillow where your beard has been.

p5c1.begin.narrate: Seven hundred percent turned out to be a conservative estimate.

The sharks had stopped bothering to hide. The bell had developed a wheeze between coughs. And the Grand Stenchmaster had been sitting in a chair in the middle of the deck since before dawn, staring at a lump under a sheet, and would not say why.

p5c1.deck: THUNK. Something large nudges the hull from underneath, the way a dog nudges a door it expects to be opened.
The bell, somewhere forward, clears its throat for nobody in particular.
hale[resigned]: Morning report, Captain. Sharks: yes. Center: somewhere. Grog: poured.
hale: Pete's got the rail patched. Mostly. Gristle's counting the stores, Salty Jim's on breakfast, and Barnacle Bob is... resting his eyes, in the crew quarters.
hale[annoyed]: In his chair, Captain. Midships. Since before the dawn watch. Looking at a sheet.
hale[resigned]: There's something under it. It hums. He says it's 'warming up'.
Beside the Forecast Board, in a chair that wasn't there yesterday, the Grand Stenchmaster sits with his hands folded on his stomach, facing a lumpy shape under an old sailcloth. The sailcloth hums.

p5c1.deck.tutorial: Make your morning rounds: the port rail (Pete), the stores (Gristle, in the Cargo Hold), the galley (Salty Jim), and the crew quarters (Barnacle Bob). Any order.
p5c1.deck.title: Another Terrible Day

then.tutorial: That's the rounds done. Everyone you've visited has been chased out by the Center. Get back up on deck.
then.title: Another Terrible Day

p5c1.pete: Pete is kneeling at the port rail with a mouthful of nails, tapping a board over a bite mark the shape of a dinner plate.
pete[tired]: Mornin', Captain. Patch number... I've stopped numbering them. This one's called Gerald.
pete: You've got to name them. Otherwise it's just wood, and you go mad.
Below him, something bumps the hull, politely, twice. Like knocking.
pete[annoyed]: They knock now. They've got MANNERS. That's worse, somehow.
captain: One bell. Outer cloud, passing the bow. Walk, don't—
He is gone. The hammer is still spinning on the deck where he dropped it. Gerald hangs off the rail by one nail.

p5c1.pete.text: It's passed! Just the edge! Passing!

p5c1.gristle: Down in the hold, Gristle is standing among the barrels with a slate and a stub of chalk, lips moving.

gristle: Forty-one sacks of biscuit. Nine casks of water. Eight casks of water. One cask of something that WAS water. Two barrels of salt pork, one barrel of salt, one barrel of pork, one barrel of 'pork'...
gristle[annoyed]: Counted, Captain. Mostly. I've been counting since the bell. Every time I get to the end, something's been eaten, spilled, or Garricked.
gristle[disgusted]: Sat on. Sampled. 'Quality assured'. There's a cheese back there with a bite out of it the size of his face.
Behind him, the treasure-room door rattles in its frame.
A thin line of yellow light creeps out underneath it, and starts to spread across the floorboards like spilled custard.
gristle[alarmed]: ...Is that door supposed to be glowing?
The slate clatters to the floor. Gristle does not.

p5c1.gristle.tutorial: The Center is coming out of the treasure room. Back up the stairs (top right).
p5c1.gristle.title: Another Terrible Day

p5c1.jim: The galley smells of porridge, smoke, and something green.
jim: Breakfast in five, Captain. Porridge. Frog Grog porridge.
mags: It was a bad theory.
jim: It was a TERRIBLE theory. But we've no fresh water left that isn't fresh Frog Grog, so it's porridge with notes of pond, or nothing.
The stovepipe gives a long, wet sigh. Something yellow begins to come DOWN it.
jim[alarmed]: Not the stove. Not the STOVE. It had the stove LAST WEEK.
The Dead Center pours out of the stove, settles over the porridge, and stays there, the way a cat sits on the one thing you were using.
jim[angry]: IT'S IN ME KITCHEN AGAIN!

p5c1.jim.tutorial: The Center is on the stove again. Out, by the ladder (top right), or down to the hold.
p5c1.jim.title: Another Terrible Day

p5c1.bob: The crew quarters are dark and close. Barnacle Bob is sitting bolt upright on a sea chest, arms folded, fast asleep.
bob: Zzz... five more minutes... five more sharks...
Behind the washroom door, somebody is humming a shanty and having a wash. You can hear the soap.
bob[surprised]: I'm up! I'm up. I was resting me eyes. They'd been open a long time, Captain.
The washroom door bangs open and Dunstan comes out of it at a speed no man in a towel should reach.
He snatches up a pillow, hugs it to his chest like a baby, and sprints.

p5c1.bob.tutorial: The Center is rolling into the sleeping quarters. Out! The ladder (top right) or the galley door.
p5c1.bob.title: Another Terrible Day

p5c1.close_call: On deck, the crew have come up from every hatch. Nobody is doing anything. Everybody is listening.
Up out of the main hatch it comes, the yellow heart of the thing, rolling toward the mainmast.
And at the foot of the mainmast, where Doc Fennimore left it to air in the morning sun: a padded basket, with a small, bald, wrapped-up parrot in it.

p5c1.close_call.say: fennimore[alarmed]: SQUAWKS! The basket! Somebody GRAB SQUAWKS!
p5c1.close_call.name: Doc Fennimore

p5c1.close_call.tutorial: Grab Squawks! His basket is at the foot of the mainmast. Then get aft, clear of the Center (the cabin-door end).
p5c1.close_call.title: Remember Squawks

p5c1.grab: You scoop him up, basket, blanket and all, and tuck him under your coat.

p5c1.grab.text: He's GOT him! He's got the bird!

p5c1.grab.tutorial: Get aft! Clear of the Center, by the cabin door.
p5c1.grab.title: Remember Squawks

p5c1.safe: You make it to the cabin door with the cloud a few steps behind. It stops at the edge of the aft deck, swirls once, and settles round the mainmast to sulk.
Everyone breathes out. Then, carefully, in again.
A tiny wisp of grey down. Then another. Then a third, very small, curled like a question mark.
They float away on the breeze, over the rail, toward the sea.

You set the basket down by the cabin door. The last of the Gust's damage is done: there is not a feather, a tuft or a wisp left on him anywhere. He is wrapped to the beak in his blanket and the little knitted sweater, and looks like a boiled egg that has been through something.

p5c1.safe.tutorial: Check on Squawks (in his basket, by the cabin door).
p5c1.safe.title: Remember Squawks

p5c1.checkin: The crew drift over in ones and twos, the way people do when nobody wants to be the first to say anything.
gristle: How're ye holding up, little mate?
You kneel down beside the basket, slowly, the way you would beside a powder keg, and lift a corner of the blanket with one finger.
In spite of everything, the corner of your mouth goes up.
fennimore[concerned]: He's eating, Captain. Sleeping. Swearing, a little more than before. Those are all good signs. He just hasn't anything left to lose.
gristle[concerned]: That's the thing, though, isn't it.
Nobody needs him to say what the thing is. Everybody on deck looks, for a moment, at the yellow haze still curled round the mainmast.
pete: That's what it did to him. One go. Feathers, the lot.
bob[sad]: That's why three bells means run. Not 'walk briskly'. Run.
gristle: I'm not ending up like— no offence, Squawks.
Round the mainmast, the yellow haze thins, loses interest, and slides off over the rail.

p5c1.checkin.tutorial: Have a word with the crew about how Squawks is doing.
p5c1.checkin.title: Remember Squawks
